newsitem.title: CHINA: China suspends loans backed by deposit receipts.
newsitem.headline: China suspends loans backed by deposit receipts.

text.p: China's central bank has issued a notice ordering the suspension of loans backed by deposit receipts and the strengthening of management over term deposits, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.

Loans backed by deposit receipts as collateral, excluding those to individuals backed by personal savings of less than 100,000 yuan ($12,000) will no longer be granted as of April 21, the People's Bank of China said in the notice.
Collateral-backed loans that have yet to mature will each be examined, the notice said.
Financial institutions will not issue receipts to units that deposit money and will instead issue a certificate to verify that the units have opened a deposit account, it said.
The certificate cannot be used for collateral, the notice said.
The central bank reiterated that receipts designed for savings deposits must not be used as collateral for deposits of units and misused receipts must be withdrawn before May 30, it said.
Post office savings are not allowed to accept deposits by units, it said.
Commercial banks must not exceed the ceiling imposed by the central bank for special receipts used for savings deposits, the notice said.
The central bank will formulate management rules on extension of loans backed by deposit receipts as collateral, and the business can only be resumed after these are issued, the notice said.
